title: MPE-seq
scope: The single MPE-seq workflow in the assigned Illumina schematic: active chromatin in isolated nuclei undergoes MPE digestion, bathophenanthroline addition, and DNA extraction. The left method vignette is illustrative. The drawn endpoint is DNA, a substrate for the sequencing reported in the primary abstract; adapter-based library construction and sequencing operations are not depicted. Neighboring DamID and Chem-seq rows and the abstract's MNase comparison are outside this target workflow.

states.label: Active chromatin in isolated nuclei
features: DNA associated with nucleosome-like particles; the figure labels the illustrative starting chromatin "Active chromatin" and the input boundary "Isolated nuclei".
The primary abstract describes genome-wide characterization by digestion of nuclei; no active-chromatin enrichment operation is drawn.

operations.label: MPE digestion
operations.description: Expose isolated nuclear chromatin to the MPE–Fe(II) cleavage reagent, converting intact chromatin DNA into digested chromatin containing DNA breaks. The figure marks this exposure with colored stars and subsequently displays fragmented chromatin.
operations.mechanism: The primary abstract reports preferential cleavage of linker DNA between nucleosomes. The matching secondary catalogue explains DNA binding by methidium intercalation and generation of single- and double-stranded breaks in the presence of oxygen.
operations.information_effect: Chromatin-dependent cleavage leaves DNA fragments that retain information about the genomic organization of nucleosomes and other protected chromatin structures. The abstract reports little sequence bias, which does not establish perfect cleavage specificity.

evidence.quote: These findings collectively indicate that MPE-seq provides a unique and straightforward means for the genome-wide analysis of chromatin structure with minimal DNA sequence bias.

operations.description: Add the named reagent to MPE-digested chromatin, producing bathophenanthroline-treated digested material. The next cartoon shows separated nucleoprotein particles. The exact chemical effect of this addition is unresolved in the registered evidence.
operations.information_effect: No new barcode, biological target association, or separate measurement is depicted. The same digested chromatin route proceeds to DNA recovery.

operations.label: DNA extraction
operations.description: Recover DNA fragments from the treated digested chromatin. The output is drawn as free DNA fragments, with the protein particles absent. The extraction block has no depicted internal substeps.
operations.information_effect: DNA fragments carry the downstream sequencing readout of chromatin structure. The abstract reports nucleosome-sized and subnucleosome-sized fragment peaks; their correlation with histones supports a possible noncanonical-chromatin interpretation without identifying the protein composition of each individual fragment. Sequencing is reported by the abstract but is not drawn as an operation here.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and the middle diagram row identify MPE-seq, expanded in the drawing as "Methidiumpropyl-EDTA sequencing (MPE-seq)". The matching catalogue heading and caption "A schematic overview of MPE-seq." confirm the target. The row has one material route and no split, pooling, or alternative assay branch. "Active chromatin" and "Isolated nuclei" describe the starting substrate; no separate cell-to-nucleus isolation transformation is resolved. The left vignette with yellow arcs has no connecting transfer arrow and introduces no additional operation. All three recorded local operations belong to the illustrated MPE-seq implementation. The primary abstract supports the cleavage/sequencing architecture, but does not establish bathophenanthroline chemistry. This unresolved reagent function does not prevent identification of the drawn route.
